title: Chief Hero
text: “How on earth did it come to this… truly hollow,” Crocodile Guy muttered from behind us, watching the proceedings alongside Éclair.
“I too find myself thinking reconciliation seems far off. Was this really the best way to resolve things? Weren’t there other options?”

Éclair looked troubled as well, but really, were we supposed to infiltrate through the underground waterways instead? Would that even have worked? I hadn’t the faintest idea, I say. And so we arrived before the tightly sealed castle gate.
“Fuhahaha! Fake heroes and fake queens! Your invasion ends here! Don’t think you can breach the mighty gates of our Melromarc!”
A knight-looking fellow declared this from atop the gate, seemingly unaware of his own insignificance. This gate—I’ve blown it up before, you know? A defensive measure as flimsy as tofu, indeed.
“Nano. Seems like there’s a pretty solid defensive spell on it, nano.”
Rival explained the magic bound to the gate.
“Normally, this is meant to activate only when the enemy has pushed this far into the kingdom, but…”
“It’s our nation’s proud defense. Think you can break through it?”
Trash asked Father, sounding rather put out.
“How very thoughtful of them… I suppose this counts as a defensive measure too, huh.”
“Bloodless surrender is already off the table at this point… let’s just blast straight through. Eagle Piercing Shot X!”
Itsuki loosed an arrow and blew the gate wide open.
“Fuhahaha! An arrow from some lowly Demi-Human like tha— wha?”
Ka-BOOM! The knight lost his voice before the utterly demolished gate.
“Is this your proud castle gate? Ha, you’re making me laugh, aren’t you? Since this is such a bother, why don’t I just blast the whole castle to smithereens with magic?”
Itsuki glanced around here and there. If he really did power up a spell and let it loose, he probably could reduce Melromarc Castle to absolutely nothing, no trace left.
“Itsuki… I get that their trash talk pissed you off, but let’s dial the threats back a notch? The queens are having trouble figuring out how to react.”
“I—I’m well aware that opposing you heroes is a mistake. I only ask that you please deal with just the enemies that need dealing with.”
“Honestly, I think you’d be better off just surrendering once you realize you haven’t got a single hero on your side…”
Ren sighed.
“There’s no backing down now, is there. Better hurry and take the castle.”
“Ah, right… let’s keep moving.”
And so we crossed through the gate and into the castle grounds.
“F-face the fake heroes and queen head on!”
“Ohhh!”
The soldiers came charging at us with a battle cry, half out of desperation. Should we just blow through all of them? Itsuki, apparently fired up too, readied his bow while still riding Father.
“The least Rival can offer is mercy, nano… sleep.”
Rival cast her spell right then.
“Ugh—!? Guh… guhhhhhh.”
The soldiers all collapsed on the spot as one, dropping like flies. A sleep spell, I say.
“Hmph…”

Trash glared at Rival for casting the spell, brows furrowed. Something about being the Staff Hero apparently meant Trash still couldn’t quite let go of certain feelings when it came to magic, or so it seemed.
“With this, the foolish soldiers who swarmed us have been neutralized, nano.”
“Shall we finish them off one by one, then, as a follow-up?”
“Itsuki?”

“I’m joking. We can’t exactly punish them for defying the royal family, can we. When the time comes to pass judgment, please do let me watch the spectacle. I’ll bring popcorn made by Naofumi-san’s group and come observe. Yes?”
“You have absolutely no intention of actually going to that, do you?! Please don’t try to drag Rabbit Guy into this!”
Itsuki tried to invite Rabbit Guy along and got flatly refused.

“Don’t be so sarcastic all the time, Itsuki… well, in the sense of defying the king, there’s not much to be done about these guys either way. Still, I’d like you to at least judge who’s actually in the right here.”
“They likely prioritized their own faith over the king, I say. Soldiers loyal to the king were probably driven out of the castle, weren’t they?”

I had no idea how many such soldiers there were, but it seemed like quite a few. Apparently the loyalty tests had been thorough, and the castle had ended up completely occupied by the Three Heroes Church.
“Still… we’ve caused this much of a ruckus, and yet not many reinforcements are coming from inside the castle.”

“Ehh… we’ve already grasped that the number of true believers in the Three Heroes Church has dwindled considerably. There have been reports of all sorts of strange occurrences happening in various regions.”
“…I see. Well then, let’s hurry to the throne room. We need to swiftly deal with that fake king sitting there.”
Father pointed Ren forward while heaping sarcasm on Trash without mercy. Ren gave a small nod in response.
“Hey, Naofumi. There’s basically no one watching anymore, right? Why don’t you take the lead. Aren’t you the Shield Hero?”
“Well, the townsfolk are already gone, so I guess that’s fine, but… Ren, aren’t you the leader of your party, being a hero and all…”
Right? Father turned to face Ren’s companions. They’d stayed quiet, but they were indeed tagging along.
“Ren-sama, as Chief Hero you really ought to be taking point here. The Shield Hero is saying the same thing, after all.”
“Quiet! This is just proper formation, that’s all!”
Ren shot back, clearly not wanting to take the lead.
“Then Motoyasu, there’s a saying about the ‘first spear’—go on, you go!”
“If that is your wish, I shall go, I say.”
“Motoyasu-kun is vetoed by my order.”
Father shut that down immediately.
“For Ren’s sake too, I’ll go up front here.”
“Then shall I ride on this rabbit fellow and take up sniping duty?”

“Theo, could I ask you to stop Itsuki’s hand from getting too quick—specifically, the kind of move where he skips straight to the movie’s climax while mid-conversation with someone during a decisive battle?”

“I feel like I sort of understand what Iwatani-sama is trying to say, but I don’t want to understand it! I’d like to decline both riding this person and stopping this person if at all possible… please stop climbing up to me with that grin, don’t come any closer!”
Itsuki hopped down off Father like some Raph-species creature and moved toward Rabbit Guy.
“There’s no need to hate it so much, is there? I’m just asking you to be my legs. Your Demi-Human form has decent visibility, you know, well suited for sniping.”
“Could you not say things where I can’t tell if you’re complimenting me or not? Maybe I should just cancel my Demi-Human transformation.”
“Oh? Wouldn’t it be better to stay like that rather than becoming some half-baked higher being?”

“I want to make myself smaller! And more to the point, please don’t do something as dangerous as riding me for sniping. Could you please stop kicking me over and over the second you climb on! You already know who your revenge target is!”
“Whoops, sorry about that—something about seeing a rabbit just makes me want to kick it these days.”
Itsuki and Rabbit Guy seemed to get along fine regardless, one way or another.
“Honestly, this isn’t playtime! Take this seriously!”
Here Ren spouted something odd—Ren, who’d dumped the whole lead role on Father the moment they’d entered the castle.
“If that’s how you feel, then perhaps you should be the one taking point.”
Itsuki tossed that back with a chuckle, dripping sarcasm.
“Honestly… I always thought he had a sharp tongue sometimes, but the cutting edge on that one was fierce.”
“Wild Bow, nano. Wild Ofumi used to crack jokes like that too sometimes, nano.”
“Gaelion-chan? Please don’t drag Motoyasu into this here, hm?”
“Continuing to joke around… I suppose this much guts is required to be a hero.”
Crocodile Guy muttered with a sigh, watching Itsuki’s antics.
“And yet, the moment he tries something clumsy, he goes berserk… the only one he’ll actually listen to is the Shield Hero, so we’ve got no choice but to rely on him.”

Itsuki really did seem prone to scattering trouble wherever he went. Quite the handful, I say. Though whether Itsuki from some other loop had been any more well-behaved was highly questionable too. Even when I’d taken preemptive measures early on, he’d screeched and hollered and shot at me plenty. Frankly, I don’t think much changes, does it? Rival’s follow-through leaves something to be desired, I say. Itsuki barely changes at all.
